name: student-illustrator-quiz
exporter: Adobe Illustrator 28.6 - Save a Copy > SVG (the legacy exporter: SVG Export Plug-In comment, .stN classes), Styling: Internal CSS, Responsive on
story: The same student drew the quiz board for the other half of the show: a question strip, four answer rows, and - because they worked out for themselves that the graphic has to look different at each moment - a pick look, a right look and a wrong look for every row plus one LUKITTU badge, all switched off in the layers panel. They named them the way the drawing reads to them: Question text, Option 1..4, Pick 1..4, Right 1..4, Wrong 1..4, Locked. Nothing here matches the words docs/SVG_AUTHORING.md section 5b suggests, because they did not read it.
idioms: Generator comment naming the SVG Export Plug-In build
Responsive export: viewBox only, no width/height attributes
<style type="text/css"> holding one property per .stN class, with two classes merged onto one selector for the badge
thirteen hidden layers exported as class="st12" whose single rule is display:none
the answer WORDS placed last in document order, under everything they must paint over
_x20_ escapes with data-name on every named layer
Nordic characters in the sample copy (Mika on Suomen korkein tunturi?, Ylläs)
whyThisMatters: The other graphic the September production ships, and the one that tests the sentence docs/SVG_AUTHORING.md section 5b prints in bold: "Naming is a shortcut, not a rule. Every one of these is a picker in the Fields step, so you can bind a file whose layers are called Group 7." Every shipped quiz sample and every existing corpus fixture uses the suggested words, so nothing until now measured the road a student who never read the page actually walks - the pickers, with no proposal arriving. If the promise holds, this file binds by hand into a working quiz; if binding it by hand is impractical, the page is making a promise the step does not keep, and that is a finding about the September production rather than about a fixture.
